keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: 'Tajikistan declared its independence on 9 September 1991', before Cliopatria's row begins in 1992. The 1992 outline is used for 1991 and overlaps the USSR's last year.

142,101 km2 against the infobox 143,100 km2 (ratio 0.99); gazetteer overlay 459 of the 481 grid cells of Natural Earth's Tajikistan inside. The civil war of 5 May 1992 to 27 June 1997 moved no outline: the Garm and Gorno-Badakhshan groups 'rose up against the newly formed government' and the south was the main zone of conflict, but nothing on the page puts any region under a separate rule on a map. The conflict is a ledger contest.
142,224 km2 (+123 km2 on 1992-99): the same 474 grid cells as the 1992 shape, a vertex-level difference only.

142,101 km2, the 1992 outline again (identical cell set). The 2011 China cession (Tajikistan 'ratified a 1999 deal (and a 2002 supplementary agreement)', areas '200 and 1,122 km2 ... respectively', 'about 0.8 percent of the country's total area') is not in the outline and the page does not locate it; the ledger records it as a loss in Gorno-Badakhshan. Russian border troops left the Afghan frontier 'until summer 2005'.
Same outline as 2006-2023. The 2025 Kyrgyz-Tajik delimitation falls after the end year.

region.text: the Tajik SSR within its Soviet-era borders, capital Dushanbe

ledger.note: 9 September 1991: Tajikistan declares independence. 'Tajikistan declared its independence on 9 September 1991', celebrated as Independence Day; the Tajik ASSR had become a union republic in 1929.

region.text: the Garm (Natural Earth 'Tadzhikistan Territories', the districts of republican subordination), Gorno-Badakhshan and southern Khatlon regions: 'The main zone of conflict was in the country's south, although disturbances occurred nationwide'

ledger.note: 5 May 1992: the Tajik civil war begins. 'Fighting broke out on 5 May 1992 between old-guard supporters of the government and a loosely organized opposition'; 'Regional groups from the Garm and Gorno-Badakhshan regions of Tajikistan rose up against the newly formed government'. The extent of opposition control is not on the page; the three regions are the researcher's reading of 'the country's south' and the named regions.

region.text: the Garm (Natural Earth 'Tadzhikistan Territories', the districts of republican subordination), Gorno-Badakhshan and southern Khatlon regions: 'The main zone of conflict was in the country's south, although disturbances occurred nationwide'

ledger.note: 27 June 1997: peace. The government and the United Tajik Opposition 'signed the General Agreement on the Establishment of Peace and National Accord in Tajikistan'; infobox '5 May 1992 – 27 June 1997', result 'Armistice'. The war killed 20,000 to 150,000 and displaced 10 to 20 percent of the population. Reviewer: confidence 2, as for the contest_start: the page dates the peace but names no land held by the opposition.

region.text: the Pamir frontier strip ceded to China, 200 km2 (1999) and 1,122 km2 (2002 agreement); 'mountainous land in the remote Pamir Mountains' on the 477 km China frontier

ledger.note: 2011: Tajikistan ratifies the China border treaties. 'In 2011, Tajikistan ratified a 1999 deal' and on 12 January the lower house 'voted to ratify the 2002 border demarcation agreement'; the cessions are '200 and 1,122 km2' respectively for the 1999 and 2002 deals, 'about 0.8 percent of the country's total area', while 'China also relinquished claims to over 28,000 km2'. The page does not locate the strip; Gorno-Badakhshan, the only province touching China, is the researcher's reading; the cession is about four to five grid cells. Reviewer: region narrowed from the whole of Gorno-Badakhshan (about 55,000 km2) to the one-cell band along the China frontier inside it (about 4,800 km2), still larger than the 1,322 km2 ceded.

region.text: the Kyrgyz-Tajik frontier, 984 km long, where the 2021 and 2022 fighting took place

ledger.note: April 2021: Kyrgyz-Tajik border fighting. 'In April 2021, a conflict over water with Kyrgyzstan escalated into one of the border clashes' (Tajikistan page); 'a three-day battle in April–May 2021, which killed 55 people' (Kyrgyzstan–Tajikistan border page).

ledger.note: May 2021: the three-day battle ends; the page gives no ceasefire date or terms.

region.text: the Kyrgyz-Tajik frontier, 984 km long, where the 2021 and 2022 fighting took place

ledger.note: 14 September 2022: renewed fighting along 'most of the border'. 'a 14–20 September confrontation that caused 137,000 Kyrgyz civilians to flee'; over 100 killed, at least 37 civilians.

ledger.note: 20 September 2022: the weeklong clashes end ('14–20 September'); no border moved.

wars.name: Tajikistani Civil War

zones.text: the Garm (Natural Earth 'Tadzhikistan Territories', the districts of republican subordination), Gorno-Badakhshan and southern Khatlon regions: 'The main zone of conflict was in the country's south, although disturbances occurred nationwide'

wars.outcome: Armistice: the General Agreement on the Establishment of Peace and National Accord in Tajikistan was signed on 27 June 1997. Infobox casualties: Russia 302 killed, 1,583 wounded; total dead 20,000 to 150,000. The opposition reorganised in Afghanistan 'with the aid of the Jamiat-i-Islami'; tens of thousands fled there.
wars.note: On 12 December 1992 the Supreme Soviet 'elected a new government under the leadership of Emomali Rahmon'; the Tajikistan page says Rahmon 'came to power ... in 1992' in its history section while its lead says the country 'has been led since 1994'. No outline of the opposition's land is on the page.

wars.name: Gorno-Badakhshan clashes (July 2012)
wars.outcome: 'Fighting erupted again, this time in and around Gorno-Badakhshan, in July 2012.' The page gives no outcome and no territorial result.
wars.note: Listed so the reviewer can see it was considered; no border moved.

wars.name: Kyrgyzstan–Tajikistan border clashes (2021 and 2022)

zones.text: the Kyrgyz-Tajik frontier, 984 km long, where the 2021 and 2022 fighting took place

wars.outcome: No ceasefire terms on the page; neither side gained land. Delimitation agreements followed in 2025 (21 February signing, 13 March agreement; Tort-Kocho road and a 15 m 'security zone' as a neutral zone), after the end year.

certainty.note: The frontier follows the Soviet republic lines; the Chinese section was undemarcated in its south ('remained undemarcated') until the 1999 and 2002 deals ratified in 2011, and the Kyrgyz section was still fought over in 2021-2022 and agreed only in 2025. The civil-war zones of 1992-1997 are contests, not borders.

notes: Four pages opened of the budget of five. The four Cliopatria shapes are one outline (identical 474 grid cells in 1992, 2000 and 2006; the +123 km2 of 2000-2005 is vertex noise), so the border story is the ledger's: the 1992-1997 civil war (contest with the United Tajik Opposition, a counterpart with no dossier), the 2011 cession to China (about 1,000 km2, unlocated), and the 2021 and 2022 clashes with Kyrgyzstan. Start 9 September 1991, not Cliopatria's 1992; a new keyframe carries 1991. The mujahideen row (1992-1995) and the Afghanistan row (1996+) are the neighbours across the Panj; the page says the opposition 'reorganized and rearmed with the aid of the Jamiat-i-Islami' in Afghanistan and Russian border troops stayed on the Afghan frontier 'until summer 2005'. Not opened (budget): the Uzbek and Afghan frontier pages, the exclaves Vorukh and Kayragach (Tajik exclaves inside Kyrgyzstan per the Kyrgyz-Tajik page), the Tajik presidents (the two pages conflict on whether Rahmon came to power in 1992 or 1994, so no rulers list). The United Tajik Opposition held land for years in some regions, but no page opened outlines it; if a rebel dossier is wanted it must be written from a page on the opposition's zones.
